newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Late weakness takes Australian bonds to lows.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Late weakness takes Australian bonds to lows.

text.p: *Australian bonds hold their softer overnight tone, more than reversing Monday's gains on some renewed late weakness
*RBA warns union body wage claim threatens accelerating wages growth to over five percent.
Some late selling into a thin market saw Australian bonds finish Tuesday near their lows and well down on their previous closes, traders said.

After weakening overnight on the back of softer U.S. Treasuries, bonds held at near their opening levels until the last hour or so of trading, when some renewed weakness saw the yield on 10-year bonds rise to near 7.50 percent.

"There's been a little bit of physical selling late in the afternoon, but you look at turnover and it doesn't need to be a huge amount of selling on a day like today to really accentuate it," one trader said.

In its monthly bulletin, The Reserve Bank in Australia (RBA) said that while enterprise based wages seemed to have plateaued and were consistent with its inflation objective, the Australian Council of Trade Unions (ACTU) wage claim could threaten this.

The RBA estimated the 'Living Wage' claim currently under consideration would, if granted, add 1.6 percentage points to wages growth, which "would take aggregate wage growth to well over five percent."
The U.S. FOMC meeting later today is the next key event for bonds, although no change in policy is expected by the market.
Locally, November merchandise imports data will be released on Wednesday. Forecasts centre on a 1.0 percent rise.
Late weakness sees spread narrowing to U.S. and Canada reversed, with long bond spread to U.S. closing at 110 for the first time in a week.
